## Review summary

- Adds startup-time `vllm:kv_cache_capacity_bytes`, with capacity preserved per global DP rank.
- Rebased onto main `36f3972812`; 30 CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit passed.
- Existing HiSparse two-pool accounting remains unsupported; see Details.

## Overview

Expose a numeric KV-cache byte-capacity Gauge for byte-based dashboards and
capacity alerts, using post-profiling `KVCacheConfig` backing sizes summed across
workers in each DP engine.

This complements #42206's group-aware token capacity and maximum concurrency
in `vllm:cache_config_info`, rather than duplicating that work. The original
duplicate-work searches found no equivalent open byte-capacity PR.

## Claims

- Counts one backing allocation per worker for dense/contiguous cache layouts,
  without double-counting aliased cache-group descriptors.
- Initializes each `engine` Gauge from its matching global-DP-rank ready response,
  independent of response arrival order.
- Computes capacity at startup with no steady-state GPU work; the Gauge uses
  the existing model/engine labels.

## Validation

Rebase validation on 2026-10-12: **30 passed** on CPU, including actual cache
packing/accounting and the reversed-DP-ready-response regression through
msgspec, `MPClient`, and the Prometheus Gauges. Changed-file pre-commit passed,
including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_kv_cache_capacity.py -q
git diff --name-only -z 36f397281295f5b58852a7eaf429b90348161079..HEAD \
  | xargs -0 pre-commit run --files
```

The original submission had 15 targeted checks covering allocation accounting,
frontend propagation, and the OpenAI serving metric inventory. Those historical
results are not a fresh GPU/full-serving validation of this rebase. The existing
engine-client test module is CUDA-alike-only and was not rerun here.

## Details

Ready responses carry the capacity from each EngineCore; the frontend stores
it by global DP rank and initializes the matching `engine` Gauge once.
`docs/design/metrics.md` documents the new metric. This rebase preserves both
the upstream prefix-cache alignment fields and the capacity field/hash exclusion;
it does not change the published metric behavior.

Known limitations, unchanged by this rebase:

- HiSparse has separate host/device pools. The current single-backing assertion
  can fail when their sizes differ, and accounting is incomplete even if equal.
  HiSparse compatibility needs a separate fix before claiming support.
- ROCm allocator tail padding to 4096 bytes is excluded from the descriptor-based
  value; this can undercount storage by less than 4096 bytes per worker. No ROCm
  runtime validation is claimed.

OpenAI Codex assisted with code, tests, documentation, and rebase maintenance.
The human submitter previously confirmed line-by-line review, understanding,
and personal execution or verification of the original tests. The new rebase
checks above were agent-run; no new human validation is implied.

Hi @heheda12345, would you have time to review this KV-cache capacity metric? It reports actual backing-allocation bytes per DP engine, enabling byte-based dashboards and alerts. The DP-rank propagation issue raised in review is addressed in `6ccc583fa4`, with a reversed-arrival regression test. I'd appreciate your feedback on the accounting and propagation. Thanks!

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

**[P2] Preserve capacity per DP engine.** Each EngineCore computes and reports its own capacity, and the ready response already carries `data_parallel_rank`. However, `_apply_ready_response()` keeps only the first non-`None` capacity in the shared `CacheConfig`, so this loop writes the first response's value to every `engine` label. DP cores profile memory independently, so their allocations can legitimately differ. Please retain capacity keyed by rank and initialize each gauge from its matching value. A two-ready-response test with ranks 0/1 and capacities 111/222 (including reversed arrival order) would catch this.

Good catch — fixed in [6ccc583fa4](https://github.com/F21HGG/vllm/commit/6ccc583fa4). The frontend now stores capacity by `data_parallel_rank`, and each `engine` gauge is initialized only from its matching entry. I added a CPU regression that delivers rank 1 / 222 before rank 0 / 111 and verifies both the stored mapping and emitted gauge values. The focused test passes (1 passed), and changed-file pre-commit passes all hooks.

@RichardoMrMu, a brief follow-up: the rank-keyed capacity fix and reversed-arrival regression are now on the PR head (`6ccc583fa4`). When convenient, could you please confirm whether this addresses the concern? Thanks again for catching it.

Apologies for the delayed reply — you asked me to confirm on 2026-09-01 and I should have answered much sooner.

Confirming: on the current head `6ccc583fa4caddd65c68333be4f9ecc397024e8b` the per-DP-engine concern is resolved. `CacheConfig.kv_cache_capacity_bytes` is now a dict keyed by global DP rank, `_apply_ready_response()` stores each engine's value under `response.data_parallel_rank` instead of keeping only the first non-`None` capacity, and `PrometheusStatLogger` initializes each engine's gauge from its matching entry.

`test_kv_cache_capacity_is_preserved_per_dp_engine` covers the ordering hazard directly: it applies rank 1 / 222 before rank 0 / 111, then asserts the stored mapping is `{0: 111, 1: 222}` and that the two gauges read 111 and 222 respectively. So arrival order no longer decides the reported capacity. That closes my finding.

As with my other reviews, this confirms the source and regression contract on this head; I have not run the functional suite, so it is not a CI claim.

+
